items.title: Parchin Military Complex, near Tehran, Iran: Tasnim news agency quoted a senior Iranian security official warning that Iranian forces would target energy infrastructure in the Middle East if the U.S. conducts strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure.
items.description: Tasnim news agency quoted a senior Iranian security official warning that Iranian forces would target energy infrastructure in the Middle East if the U.S. conducts strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure.
items.rawSummary: The Parchin military complex near Tehran remains under scrutiny as a U.S. air campaign targets IRGC assets across Iran, while the regime’s opaque leadership, hardline decision-making, and threats of retaliatory strikes on regional energy infrastructure deepen the uncertainty.
items.analysis: The Parchin military complex near Tehran has not been directly confirmed as a strike target despite a broad U.S. bombing campaign that began on July 30, with CENTCOM releasing footage of two waves of airstrikes on dozens of IRGC military sites. The Times reported that the CIA and Mossad are intensifying efforts to locate Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, who is believed to be in an underground shelter near Tehran or Qom and has not been seen publicly since a February 2026 airstrike, with the search shifting from cyber to human intelligence amid suspicions that the IRGC may be concealing his death. In parallel, The Telegraph detailed that U.S. and Israeli officials are considering a land blockade to strangle Iran’s economy, while CNN cited U.S. officials saying the IRGC has seized complete wartime decision-making, sidelining moderates and signaling a prolonged conflict. Late on July 31, Tasnim news agency quoted a senior Iranian security official warning that Iranian forces would target energy infrastructure in the Middle East if the U.S. hits Iranian energy sites, raising the stakes for further escalation.

items.title: Qeshm Island and Strait of Hormuz coast, Iran, Iran: UKMTO said the tanker attack occurred in the southern shipping lane near Oman.
items.description: UKMTO said the tanker attack occurred in the southern shipping lane near Oman.
items.rawSummary: Hostilities continue in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran striking commercial vessels and claiming to have closed the waterway, while the U.S. disputes those claims and reports that traffic has fallen to about 10% of pre-war levels.
items.analysis: Hostilities escalated sharply after a U.S. strike on Qeshm Island killed three IRGC members, which Iranian state media said hit a residential area. Iran claimed retaliatory ballistic missile strikes on Al-Azraq airbase destroyed three U.S. F-35 jets, but CENTCOM denied any damage, stating all missiles were intercepted or failed to reach their targets, and described IRGC assertions as part of an ongoing disinformation campaign. The IRGC has repeatedly warned that the strait will remain shut unless U.S. provocations cease and has claimed to have struck and halted two oil tankers that ignored warnings, causing four others to turn back. In a contrasting development, Pakistan reportedly secured Iranian cooperation to escort a Qatari LNG carrier through the strait, signaling limited willingness to negotiate passage with non-belligerent parties. Adding a civilian administrative layer to the closure, the Persian Gulf Waterway Management Organization announced that transit is not possible due to continued aggressive U.S. military actions and that requests will be reviewed gradually once stability returns, reinforcing the government's narrative that Washington is responsible for the disruption. CENTCOM has continued to insist that the primary threat to shipping comes from the IRGC itself, and in its latest fact check acknowledged that commercial traffic has fallen to around 10% of pre-war levels while noting that some vessels using a U.S.-established safety corridor have been attacked by Iran; it also reiterated that Iran does not control the strait and thousands of ships have transited in recent months. The persistent danger was underscored overnight when UKMTO reported that a tanker was struck by a projectile in its engine room while using a U.S.-guarded route in the southern shipping lane near Oman, leaving it not under command.

items.title: Vizar plant, Kyiv region, Ukraine: Overnight Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv killed 9 people and injured 27, including 4 children, causing fires and widespread damage across multiple districts.
items.description: Overnight Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv killed 9 people and injured 27, including 4 children, causing fires and widespread damage across multiple districts.
items.rawSummary: The Vizar drone factory, a U.S.-owned facility producing AI-guided drones, was destroyed by a Russian ballistic missile, and persistent ballistic strikes on Kyiv have killed civilians, with the latest overnight attack leaving 9 dead and 27 injured.
items.analysis: The Vizar drone factory, owned by U.S.-based Terminal Autonomy and producing AI-guided attack drones, was destroyed by a Russian ballistic missile in what The Guardian characterized as the first known Russian strike on a U.S.-owned company in Ukraine. The plant supported a deep-strike drone campaign against Russia, which the Financial Times reports is aided by U.S. and French intelligence mapping air defense networks. Amid this, President Zelensky secured U.S. licensing support for local Patriot interceptor production, though supplies remain constrained by the conflict with Iran. Diplomatic tensions with Iran had earlier eased after assurances that an attack on an Iranian ship was unintentional. Kyiv has continued to face lethal ballistic missile attacks, with a strike on July 31 killing fleeing civilians, and an overnight attack on August 1 killing 9 and wounding 27, including children.
